observed_behavior: The HTML dialog focusing steps first stop when the document's allow-focus steps disallow focusing; otherwise, a dialog with autofocus is selected as the focus control, or if absent the dialog's focus delegate is used, falling back to the dialog itself. The algorithm invokes focusing steps on that control and applies further top-document autofocus bookkeeping only under its origin/context checks. The author-facing text recommends autofocus on the intended initial descendant, or on the dialog if no such descendant exists.
context: W07 B2 K3 read-only observation; WHATWG HTML Living Standard authoritative for the described native HTML mechanisms and guarded algorithms only; source shows Last Updated 20 July 2026.
limitations: The spec distinguishes algorithmic fallback from contextual author choice; it does not promise first input, first button, or destructive action as a universal initial focus.
The focus operation can do nothing when the chosen control is not focusable; the algorithm has early-return/origin conditions.
The dialog lifecycle also stores a previously focused element and has conditional restoration on close, not an unconditional focus-return guarantee.
No keyboard focus or user-experience result was experimentally observed.
